note: Editorial copy only. Every number on the site is generated from results/ by scripts/build_site.py. Do not put measurements in this file.

site.name: WhichJudge
site.headline: You don't need a better model. You need a quit line.
site.description: Independent bake-off of cheap in-loop decision models. Jev vs gpt-4o-mini vs TF-IDF on 8 classification decisions, n=500 frozen public gold, full per-call receipts.

tasks.title: Consumer complaint routing
tasks.replaces: LLM classifier routing inbound financial complaints to a product queue
tasks.dataset: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database, 8 product queues
tasks.labels: credit_reporting / debt_collection / cards / bank_account / mortgage / money_transfer / loans / student_loan
tasks.why: The only row here that is not academic gold: a regulator runs this routing live and the consumer writes the narrative. Jev 82.8% and Mini 81.0% are tied (p=0.25), and TF-IDF beats both at 86.8%. Narratives average about 240 tokens, so this is also the first row where Jev is the cheaper API: $33.89 against $53.21 per million decisions.
tasks.gate: At >=0.7: 88.2% on 88.0% of complaints. ECE 0.100 is borderline, and the 0.9 bin is the weak spot, so gate at 0.9 (91.8% on 75.6%) if a misroute is expensive.

tasks.title: Comment toxicity gate
tasks.replaces: Toxicity classifier gating user comments before publication
tasks.why: The same decision as the hate-speech row, on clean CC0 gold. Here the two models tie: Jev 78.0% and Mini 77.0% (p=0.69). TF-IDF wins again at 82.8%. Read this next to the hate row: the Don't verdict there does not survive a change of gold, so it was a fact about that dataset more than about Jev.
tasks.gate: Calibration is usable here (ECE 0.075) unlike the hate row. At >=0.8: 91.3% on 52.8% of comments. Publish that half automatically and queue the rest.

tasks.title: SMS spam gate
tasks.replaces: Spam vs ham classifier on inbound SMS
tasks.why: Dead heat: Jev 96.4, Mini 96.4, TF-IDF 96.4. Classical ML is enough here. Nothing separates the three.
tasks.gate: No accuracy reason to switch either way. At >=0.7: 98.9% on 88.8% of traffic.

tasks.title: Review polarity
tasks.why: Tied (McNemar p=0.55). 97.0% vs 96.4%. TF-IDF drops to 82.6%, so the models earn their keep against classical, not against each other.
tasks.gate: Best-calibrated task on the board (ECE 0.015). At >=0.7: 98.5% on 91.8% of reviews.

tasks.title: Message emotion
tasks.why: Jev +4.8pt, McNemar p=0.0053. Optimism vs joy is still the messy pair. TF-IDF trails badly at 64.2%.
tasks.gate: Use Jev in-loop. At >=0.7: 88.5% on 74.8% of traffic.

tasks.title: Offensive language screen
tasks.why: Jev +5.8pt, McNemar p=0.0079. Mean confidence is only 0.75, so the gate is the product, not the headline accuracy.
tasks.gate: Auto at >=0.9 (89.0% on 50.8%). At >=0.7 it is 84.4% on 68.0%. Rest to a human.

tasks.title: Social sentiment (3-way)
tasks.why: Coin flip vs Mini (p=0.58). Neutral is still the killer class. ECE 0.141 means the confidence number is shaky too.
tasks.gate: Jev if confidence >=0.7 (80.6% on 74.2%); Mini or a human on the rest.

tasks.title: News topic
tasks.why: TF-IDF 90.8% beats Jev 85.6% and Mini 82.6% after training on 120k rows. Among the APIs Jev wins by 3.0pt (p=0.0093). If you have labels, skip both models.
tasks.gate: Jev first among APIs. At >=0.7: 90.1% on 90.6% of articles.

tasks.title: Banking queue routing
tasks.labels: cards / top_up / cash_atm / transfers / fx / account / payments_fees / other
tasks.why: TF-IDF 93.2% beats both neural judges (p<1e-19) if you have labels. Jev still beats Mini among APIs by 7.4pt. Do not pay for a model on this task if you can train one.
tasks.gate: ECE 0.213, the worst on the board: do not auto-route on confidence here. At >=0.7 it is only 74.9% on 91.0%.

tasks.title: Hate-speech screen
tasks.why: Mini +7.8pt (p=0.0026). Jev mean confidence 0.67 and ECE 0.187, so the confidence cannot carry a threshold either. Kept on the homepage, but compare it with the Civil Comments row: on cleaner gold for the same decision the gap disappears.
tasks.gate: If you insist: >=0.9 is 81.6% but only 32.6% coverage. Keep a specialist.

reproduce.heading: Reproduce this and I will publish your numbers
reproduce.body: Receipts prove I did not edit my own table. They cannot prove the APIs said it, because in principle I could have written the receipts. Only someone else re-running it fixes that. Clone the repo, add your own keys, run scripts/run_eval.py, and send me the summary.json diff. It costs about $0.12 in API calls. Confirmed runs get a reproduced-by line on the row, credited however you want.
reproduce.subject: WhichJudge reproduction

contribute.heading: Have labelled data for a real decision?
contribute.body: Every task here is public academic gold, which is comparable but not production. The decisions worth measuring are the ones people actually run: support-queue routing, prompt-injection screening, PR risk gating, refund eligibility. Those need labelled examples, and nobody has published them. If you have a few hundred rows you can share, or a public set worth adding, I will measure it and publish the row. Your data does not get republished unless you say so.
contribute.subject: WhichJudge dataset
